# Intake Brief — Validate all card text (CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0)

## Problem statement

The integer-economy migration (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6) scaled coin/reputation
**data** ×100 but only partially updated the **card text**. Business,
community-space, upgrade, and staff `description` fields were scaled, but every
event `effect` field was left at its pre-migration display-scale value (e.g.
`evt-festival` reads `+2 coins` while its `coinDelta` is `200`), and
`evt-shopping-spree` still shows a fractional `+2.5 coins` (data `250`).
Players therefore read card text that disagrees with the amount the engine
actually applies, with the activity log, and with the raw-integer HUD. The
same stale values also remain in every other player-visible surface that
repeats card coin/reputation amounts — card-face SVGs, tooltips, tutorial copy,
staff-skill descriptions, and the `docs/main-street/*` reference material.

## Users

- **Player** — needs each card's text to state the same coin/reputation amount
  that will actually be applied, so purchase/play decisions are informed.
- **Game designer / balancer** — needs `card-data.csv` text and data columns to
  agree so balancing is based on accurate descriptions.
- **Developer / QA** — needs a durable check that catches future card-text/data
  drift instead of relying on manual review.

### User stories

- As a player, when I read an event card's effect text I see the same
  coin/reputation amount that the game applies and that the activity log shows.
- As a designer, I can trust that every card description matches its
  `card-data.csv` values without mental ×100 conversion.
- As a developer, a failing check tells me exactly which card's text no longer
  matches its data.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Every player-visible card-text surface is ×100-consistent with card
   data.** Every numeric coin/reputation mention in card text equals the
   corresponding data column (`coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`,
   `reputationPerTurn`, `ongoingCost`, `reputationBonus`, `incomeBonus`,
   staff-skill magnitudes) under the documented ×100 scale. The audited
   surfaces are: the `card-data.csv` `description` and `effect` columns;
   card-face SVG text (`MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and committed SVG
   artifacts); tooltips (`MainStreetFormatting.ts`); tutorial copy
   (`TutorialFlow.ts`, `i18n/tutorial-en.ts`); staff-skill descriptions
   (`MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`); and the `docs/main-street/*` reference
   material. All event `effect` texts are scaled (e.g. `evt-festival`
   `+2 coins` → `+200 coins`); `evt-shopping-spree` `+2.5 coins` →
   `+250 coins`. No fractional coin/reputation value remains in any
   player-visible card text.
2. **Non-coin/reputation numbers are unchanged.** Percentages (`45%`, `90%`,
   `120%`), durations (`3 turns`), hand-slot counts, levels, and the
   `{SYNERGY_RATE}` token are out of scope and verified unchanged.
3. **Automated regression test guards against drift.** An automated unit test
   parses every card's text coin/reputation mentions and asserts they match the
   card's data columns under the documented ×100 scale, failing with a message
   that identifies the offending card. The test must run in the `unit` profile
   and fail if a future edit desynchronises card text from card data.
4. **Tests and artifacts updated.** Existing test expectations that reference
   old text values are updated; committed card SVG artifacts are regenerated to
   match the corrected text; `npm run build` and the unit test profile pass.
5. **Documentation updated.** Every doc carrying stale fractional card values
   (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and the other `docs/main-street/*` files
   identified during implementation) is revised to the integer scale; code
   comments describing the old scale (e.g. the `{bonus}` example `+2 coins` in
   `TutorialFlow.ts`) are corrected. All related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki
   or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Source of truth is `card-data.csv`.** Text is corrected to match data; data
  values are not changed to match text.
- **Only coin/reputation amounts scale.** Percentage, rate, duration, and count
  values are untouched; `{SYNERGY_RATE}` stays a rate token resolved at render
  time.
- **Cover every player-visible surface (producer-confirmed).** Card-face SVGs,
  tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions, and docs are all in scope,
  not just the CSV `description`/`effect` columns.
- **Automated tests required (producer-confirmed).** The regression guard is an
  automated unit test, not a manual checklist.
- **No rebalancing.** Apply text-only ×100 corrections; any balance change is a
  separate work item.
- **CHANGELOG.md excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `card-data.csv` business/community-space/upgrade/staff `description` fields
  were scaled ×100 by CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6.
- Every event `effect` field retains its pre-migration value (small integers),
  while `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` were scaled ×100 — e.g. `evt-festival`
  `effect: "+2 coins to all Culture businesses and +1 reputation."`,
  `coinDelta: 200`, `reputationDelta: 100`.
- `evt-shopping-spree` is the only card with a fractional value in text:
  `"+2.5 coins to all Commerce businesses."` (`coinDelta: 250`).
- The HUD renders raw integers (`Coins: 1000`); the activity log renders raw
  integers via `describeEventEffects` (`+200 coins`); SpecificSynergy event
  tooltips show only the (small) `effect` text, so the mismatch is visible to
  players.
- `TutorialFlow.ts` resolves `{bonus}` from `coinDelta` (`+${coinDelta} coins`
  → `+200 coins`) but its doc comment still says `e.g. '+2 coins'`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (and several other `docs/main-street/*`
  files, including `specialization-skills.md`, `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`,
  `the-build-gdd.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`,
  `content-design-and-progression.md`, and `prd-multi-use-card-economy.md`)
  still use fractional values such as `+0.4/turn` and `0.25 coins/turn`.
- No automated test currently compares card text amounts against card data;
  existing card tests (`event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`,
  `card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `card-schema-validation.test.ts`,
  `csv-checksum.test.ts`) use synthetic fixtures.

## Desired change

Audit every player-visible card-text source — CSV text, card-face SVGs,
tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions, and docs — scale all
coin/reputation amounts to match the integer data (×100), remove the last
fractional value, add an automated regression test so text/data drift is caught
automatically, and refresh stale docs and comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — scale every event `effect` coin/rep
  amount ×100 and fix the `evt-shopping-spree` fractional value; check remaining
  `description` fields.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — tooltip rendering of
  `effect`/`description`; confirm text/data consistency.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — card-face
  text; confirm integer rendering and regenerate committed SVG artifacts.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — staff-skill
  descriptions; verify already-scaled values.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — `{bonus}` doc comment and any
  tutorial card-value copy.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — tutorial copy referencing
  card coin/reputation values.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — HUD tooltip coin/rep
  values and card detail lines.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` — committed card-face SVG
  artifacts; regenerate after text corrections.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and the other `docs/main-street/*` files
  with stale fractions — update to the integer scale.
- `tests/main-street/**` — new automated card-text/data consistency test plus
  updated expectations.

## Related work

- **Potentially related docs**
  - `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — canonical card text/data source.
  - `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — card catalogue with stale fractional values.
  - `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — card tooltip text builder.
  - `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — card-face SVG text.
  - `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — `{bonus}` interpolation and stale comment.
  - `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — staff-skill descriptions.
- **Potentially related work items**
  - `Move to integer numbers for coins and reputation (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6)` —
    completed; the migration whose text updates this item validates.
  - `Dynamic synergy bonus text on business cards (difficulty-aware percentage, Option B) (CG-0MS9GS91E004OAF4)` —
    completed; dynamic card text rendering.
  - `Synergy bonus on business cards (CG-0MRXYHNHB006F0U9)` — completed;
    synergy text semantics.
  - `In main street log should show total effects (CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ)` —
    completed; log integer deltas that already disagree with event text.
  - `Main Street tutorial: full text review and step restructure (CG-0MSKSJ9SS0069ZWT)` —
    completed; tutorial copy review precedent.
  - `Fix card rendering, UI overlay, and formatting tests (CG-0MTKLQ1P40091YTH)` —
    completed; card rendering/formatting tests.
  - `Main Street Game over dialog is not showing text (CG-0MQ2IL40S0060FUG)` —
    completed; card/dialog text rendering precedent.
  - `Implement Multi-Use Card Economy in Main Street (CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7)` —
    completed; card-economy semantics behind the coin/rep values.
  - `Docs: tutorial-localization + README updates (CG-0MSLXJ1OK004LJKU)` —
    completed; tutorial/doc text-update precedent.

> **Automated related-work report:** `/skill:find-related` was run and inserted
> a report into the work item. Its findings are folded into the list above.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: event `effect` scaling direction (confirmed ×100).** Producer
  confirmed event effect text scales ×100 to match `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`,
  consistent with the already-scaled business descriptions and the raw-integer
  HUD/log. The regression test encodes this.
- **Risk: natural-language parsing fragility.** Comparing text amounts to data
  columns requires parsing prose. Mitigation: constrain the test to well-formed
  `[+-]?N coins?` / `[+-]?N reputation` patterns and/or an explicit per-card
  expected-value map, with a clear failure message naming the card.
- **Risk: scope creep into rebalancing.** Mitigation: apply only ×100 text
  corrections; file a separate balance work item for any value change.
- **Risk: missed text sources.** Coin/reputation copy lives in CSV text, SVGs,
  tooltips, tutorial strings, staff skills, and docs. Mitigation: grep the repo
  for fractional coin/rep patterns and for the `effect`/`description` columns,
  and regenerate committed SVG artifacts.
- **Risk: expanded scope increases effort.** Producer confirmed "cover
  everything" and automated tests, which widens the surface beyond the CSV and
  raises the estimate. Mitigation: effort/risk re-estimated after the scope
  confirmation.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** scope covers every player-visible surface that
  repeats card coin/reputation amounts (CSV text, SVGs, tooltips, tutorial
  copy, staff skills, docs); percentages, durations, and counts are out of
  scope.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** the regression guard is an automated unit test.
- **Assumption:** documentation updates cover the docs carrying stale card
  coin/reputation values; unrelated doc drift is out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

An initial brief was drafted from the seed context, then three clarifying
questions were put to the producer and answered (2026-09-24, interactive
reply). The brief has been updated to the confirmed answers.

- **Q: Should event `effect` text be scaled ×100 to match
  `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` (e.g. `+2 coins` → `+200 coins`)?** —
  **Answer (producer): yes.** Source: interactive reply; consistent with the
  already-scaled business descriptions and the raw-integer HUD/log. Research:
  `git show 192943c9` showed the migration scaled descriptions but not the
  event `effect` column; `MainStreetRendererHud.ts` and
  `MainStreetStateLog.ts` render raw integers.
- **Q: Is "all card text" limited to the `card-data.csv` `description`/`effect`
  columns, or should it cover tooltips/SVGs/tutorial copy/docs too?** —
  **Answer (producer): cover everything.** Source: interactive reply. The brief
  now scopes card-face SVGs, tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions,
  and `docs/main-street/*`.
- **Q: Is an automated regression test the expected way to "ensure" ongoing
  correctness, or is a one-time audit-and-fix sufficient?** —
  **Answer (producer): automated tests.** Source: interactive reply. AC3 is now
  a required automated unit test rather than a manual checklist.

**Research summary:** `wl show CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 --json` established the
migration contract (CSV ×100, integer-only UI). `git show 192943c9` confirmed
the migration scaled business/community/staff/upgrade descriptions but did not
touch the event `effect` column. A CSV parse of all 173 rows found exactly one
remaining fractional text value (`evt-shopping-spree`, `+2.5 coins` vs
`coinDelta=250`) and showed every event `effect` still at display scale
(e.g. `evt-festival` `+2 coins` vs `coinDelta=200`). `MainStreetFormatting.ts`,
`MainStreetStateLog.ts` (`describeEventEffects`), `MainStreetRendererHud.ts`,
`TutorialFlow.ts`, and `MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` were inspected to map the
text sources and confirm the HUD/log render raw integers. `docs/main-street/*`
was grepped and found to retain fractional values in `card-catalog.md` and
several other files. Existing tests (`event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`,
`card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `card-schema-validation.test.ts`,
`csv-checksum.test.ts`) use synthetic data and contain no card-text/data
consistency guard. The producer's three answers (×100 direction, cover
everything, automated tests) were applied to the problem statement, AC1/AC3/AC5,
constraints, and risks.

# Keep tooltips within screen bounds

## Problem statement

Tooltips are rendered at a fixed offset from the hover point without any viewport-bounds checking. When a hovered element sits near the right or bottom edge of the window, the tooltip overflows the viewport; in the DOM-rendered mode this extends the document's scrollable area, so the page "resizes to make space" (scrollbars appear / layout shifts). The tooltip must always be positioned so that it is fully visible and never alters the document layout.

## Users

- **Players** hovering cards, HUD elements, and buttons in Main Street, Lost Cities, Sushi Go, and the Gym tooltip/Gym-card-index demos.
- **Engine consumers (game developers)** who rely on the shared `TooltipManager` (DOM and Phaser modes) so they do not have to re-implement bounds handling per game.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I hover a card near the right edge of the screen, the tooltip appears fully on-screen instead of being clipped or pushing the page wider.
- As a player, showing a tooltip never causes the game canvas or page to jump/resize.
- As a game developer, when I supply a `phaserRender` callback I can clamp my tooltip into the game canvas with a shared helper rather than copying clamp maths between games.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **DOM-mode clamping:** For a hover point near each of the four viewport edges, the DOM tooltip's rendered bounding rectangle is fully inside the browser viewport (`left >= 0`, `top >= 0`, `right <= window.innerWidth`, `bottom <= window.innerHeight`), with a small margin. Verified by a browser (`*.browser.test.ts`) test in `tests/ui/`.
2. **No document resize:** Showing (and hiding) a DOM tooltip does not change the document scroll size — no horizontal/vertical scrollbar is introduced (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` before and after `show()`). Verified by a browser test.
3. **Phaser-mode clamping:** The shared Phaser render callbacks keep their tooltip containers inside the game canvas bounds (`0..GAME_W` × `0..GAME_H`) at all four edges. Gym's callback (currently unclamped) is brought in line with the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, ideally via a shared, unit-tested helper. Verified by unit tests (helper) plus the existing scene/browser tests.
4. **No regression to existing positioning:** Existing world→screen coordinate mapping (canvas scale, canvas offset, camera scroll) and the settings `showTooltips` toggle behaviour are preserved; the existing `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` / `TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` expectations are updated rather than weakened.
5. **Validation and documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (tooltip component section) and any relevant Gym help text. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies.
- Must not regress reduced-motion, `pointer-events: none`, or the maximum `z-index` behaviour of the DOM tooltip.
- Must remain safe in non-DOM environments (`document`/`window` undefined) and when the canvas bounding rect cannot be read — fall back to hiding, as today.
- Clamping must be cheap (measure once per `show()`, no per-frame layout thrash, no resize listeners).
- The DOM tooltip node must not contribute to the document's scrollable overflow area.
- Use UK English in comments and docs; escape only backticks in worklog content.
- Existing tests that assert `div.style.position === 'absolute'` will need updating if the positioning strategy changes (see Risks).

## Existing state

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — `TooltipManager`. DOM mode computes `screenX`/`screenY` from the canvas rect, camera scroll, and scale, then sets `left`/`top` = point + `(10, 10)` offset with **no bounds check**. The node is `position: absolute`, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: 2147483647`, `max-width: 320px`, appended to `document.body`. Phaser mode delegates layout entirely to the caller's `phaserRender` callback.
- Consumers in DOM mode: Main Street (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` constructs it; `MainStreetRendererStreet/Hud/Market/Layout.ts` call `show`), `GymTooltipScene` DOM half, `GymCardIndexScene`.
- Consumers in Phaser mode: `LostCitiesScene.ts` (`createTooltipManager`) and `SushiGoScene.ts` — both already clamp with `Phaser.Math.Clamp(..., 4, GAME_W - boxW - 4)` etc. `GymTooltipScene`'s Phaser callback does **not** clamp.
- Tests: `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` (unit), `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` (browser, asserts `position === 'absolute'`), `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` (SLL anchors only), plus Main Street tooltip content tests.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents `TooltipManager`; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` maps the tooltip scenes.

## Desired change

- Add viewport-bounds clamping to the shared DOM tooltip renderer in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`:
  - Position the node relative to the viewport so it cannot extend the document scroll area (e.g. `position: fixed`).
  - Measure the node after setting content, then flip it above/left of the hover point when there is not enough room below/right, and clamp to the viewport as a final guard, keeping a small margin.
  - Keep the existing world→screen conversion (canvas rect + camera scroll + scale).
- Extract a reusable bounds-clamping helper for in-canvas (Phaser) tooltips, mirroring the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, and use it in `GymTooltipScene` (and optionally migrate Lost Cities / Sushi Go to the shared helper with no behaviour change).
- Add unit tests for the clamp maths (all four edges, both axes, oversized tooltip) and browser tests proving the tooltip stays in the viewport and does not change document scroll size.
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and Gym help text if the scene behaviour/description changes).
- **Test-first:** author the clamp-helper unit tests and the browser edge/document-scroll tests before wiring the DOM renderer and the Gym callback, so the new behaviour is specified by failing tests first.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — Add DOM-mode viewport clamping / anti-resize positioning; export a reusable Phaser-mode clamp helper.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — Apply the clamp helper in the `phaserRender` callback (currently unclamped).
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — Unit tests for clamp maths via the DOM mock and helper.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — Edge-position + document-scroll-size assertions; update the `position` selector assumption.
- `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` — Extend with Gym Phaser-mode in-bounds assertions (if the scene callback is changed).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the bounds guarantee for both tooltip modes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the correct, complete interpretation of the title is "no tooltip (in either DOM or Phaser mode) may render outside its visible bounds", not just the DOM overlay. The DOM mode is the cause of the reported page-resize; Phaser mode only clips. Recommended and assumed.
- **Assumption:** clamping (shift/flip to stay visible) is preferred over truncating content or shrinking the tooltip. Documented assumption; trivially revisitable.
- **Risk:** switching the DOM node to `position: fixed` invalidates the existing browser test's `position === 'absolute'` selector — update the selector to target the tooltip by its stable attributes (`pointer-events: none` + `z-index`) rather than `position`.
- **Risk:** measuring the node to clamp requires it to be laid out; setting `display: block` before measuring may cause a one-frame flash. Mitigate by measuring immediately after content is set and before paint (single synchronous reflow), or measure with `visibility: hidden` then reveal.
- **Risk:** `window`/`document` may be undefined in unit tests/SSR — guard clamping behind the existing `document` checks and fall back to the unclamped path (or hide) when dimensions are unavailable.
- **Risk:** double clamping when a game's `phaserRender` already clamps — the helper must be opt-in and not re-apply automatically to caller-managed containers.
- **Risk:** oversized tooltips (taller/wider than the viewport) cannot fit; clamp to the margin and accept partial visibility, documenting the behaviour.
- **Scope-creep risk:** tooltip content wrapping/truncation, touch/long-press tooltips, and tooltip theming are out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Related work

- **CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7** – Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover (completed) — introduced the shared `TooltipManager` this bug affects.
- **CG-0MODIX70W002JXQN** – `feat(ui): add TooltipManager` / `fix(ui): DOM-positioned tooltip displays above cards` — prior DOM coordinate-mapping work in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`.
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed) — SLL precedent for declarative positioning.
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed) — SLL layout system; relevant if bounds handling is expressed via SLL zones.
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed) — Main Street tooltip content fix, no overlap with positioning.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed)
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ake, bounds, displayed, ensure, keep (+11 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+10 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+7 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q:** Are there open questions requiring producer input? — **A:** No. The seed context ("Sometimes when a tooltip is displayed it would render outside the screen bounds. This results in the screen resizing to make space. We need to ensure that the tooltip is positioned such that it stays within screen bounds.") plus repository research was sufficient to draft a clear, testable brief. No interview round was required. Source: seed context supplied with the intake invocation + repo inspection.

**Prior related answers:** none.

**Research summary:** Inspected `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` (DOM node is `position: absolute` on `document.body` with no bounds check — the resize cause; Phaser mode delegates to `phaserRender`), the four in-repo consumers (Main Street, Gym DOM, Gym Phaser, Lost Cities, Sushi Go), and the existing tests/docs. Lost Cities and Sushi Go already clamp inside the canvas with `Phaser.Math.Clamp`; Gym and the DOM renderer do not. No existing shared clamp helper exists. Related completed tooltip work items were found via `wl search` (see automated report).

# Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (WL-0MTH6B20C002ZOM2) — Intake brief

## Problem statement

The Pawn Shop business card (`biz-pawnshop`, Main Street game, `Tableau-Card-Engine`) is currently **increasing** the player's reputation by +5 per turn and costs 300 coins to purchase — both incorrect per design intent. A pawn shop should be a low-reputation, budget-friendly establishment: it should **reduce** reputation by 0.1 per turn and be cheaper to acquire (200 coins at the ×100 scale, i.e. 2.00 in game terms).

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I expect placing a Pawn Shop on my street to slightly harm my reputation each turn (`-0.1`), not boost it, so that reputation decisions involve meaningful trade-offs.
- **As a player**, I expect the Pawn Shop to remain an accessible budget business (cheaper than the 300-coin tier-2 group) despite its per-turn reputation penalty.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect CSV card data and tests to stay internally consistent (numeric columns valid; ongoing-cost convention preserved).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Negative reputation per turn.** `biz-pawnshop.reputationPerTurn` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` changes from `5` to `-10` (the ×100 integer-economy representation of the design value −0.1; see CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6); placing the Pawn Shop on the street grid accrues a **negative** reputation delta (−10) during the income phase (`applyIncome`), never a positive one.
2. **Reduced purchase cost.** `biz-pawnshop.cost` in the CSV changes from `300` to `200`; the market purchase price for the Pawn Shop is 200 (2.00 at the ×100 display convention).
3. **Synergy opt-out unchanged.** The Pawn Shop still provides and receives **zero** synergy bonuses (`synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, no adjacency synergy) — unchanged behaviour (existing tests in `adjacency.test.ts` / `MainStreetHandSynergy.test.ts` still pass).
4. **Test coverage.** Add or extend automated tests asserting (a) the Pawn Shop's negative per-turn reputation and (b) its updated cost of 200; the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (card tooltips/descriptions generated from CSV, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` and any README/wikis as applicable, including code comments). Note: `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- CSV numeric columns are validated by `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (`parseFloat`); `-0.1` is a valid numeric value.
- Costs use the ×100 integer convention (200 = 2.00 coins); `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw at income time (no ×100) — confirm via tests during implementation.
- **Do not** regenerate costs via the balance-cards curve tool (`src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts`): it would reassign tier bands. Its Pawn Shop special case (cost −2) applies only when `baseIncome === 0`, which is not our case — no algorithm change needed.
- Ongoing-cost convention (documented in `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts`) is `max(25, cost / 4)`. **Assumption (producer to confirm):** if `cost` becomes 200, `ongoingCost` follows the convention to 50 (currently 75). The producer's clarification specified only the purchase cost; do not change `ongoingCost` unless confirmed.

## Existing state

Current `biz-pawnshop` row in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`:

```
business,biz-pawnshop,Pawn Shop,300,230,Commerce,...,1,5,0,0,Trades second-hand goods. Does not provide or receive synergy bonuses.,2,...,75,...
```

- `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 230`, `reputationPerTurn = 5`, `synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, `tier = 2`, `ongoingCost = 75`.

| Field | Current | Desired |
|---|---|---|
| `reputationPerTurn` | `5` | `-10` (×100 integer economy; reduces reputation by 0.1/turn in design terms) |
| `cost` | `300` | `200` (2.00 at ×100) |
| `ongoingCost` | `75` | `50` — **assumption**, follows `cost/4` convention; pending confirmation |
| `synergyCoinBonus` / `synergyRepBonus` / `tier` / `baseIncome` | `0` / `0` / `2` / `230` | unchanged |

## Risks & assumptions

- **Ongoing-cost convention (assumption, unconfirmed).** Changing `cost` to 200 implies `ongoingCost = 50` per the documented `max(25, cost/4)` convention; the producer's clarification only covered the purchase cost. Implementer should confirm before touching `ongoingCost`; leaving it at 75 leaves a convention inconsistency (risk: low).
- **Unit conventions.** Costs are ×100 integers; `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw. If the game's ×100 scaling applies to reputation in the current branch, `-0.1` may need to be stored as `-10` — validate against the repo's existing tests before finalising the CSV value (risk: medium; mitigated by AC1's negative-delta assertion).
- **Do not regenerate balances.** Running the balance-cards tool would reassign the Pawn Shop's tier band and overwrite the manual cost; the change is a data-only edit plus tests.
- **Scope-creep guard.** The Pawn Shop's card *description* text could mention its reputation penalty, but that is an extra opportunity — record as a linked work item if desired, not part of this item's scope.

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — template loading from CSV (read-only; verifies `-0.1` and `200` parse)

- `src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts` — no change expected (verify special case is unaffected)

Or some other cost field? The reputation change (from +5 to −0.1 per turn) is clear."

# Chore: Document config-driven game catalogue + create per-game build presets

## Problem statement

The config-driven game catalogue (`configs/*.json` presets + `GAMES_CONFIG`)
is only described briefly and in two places (README and the Developer Guide),
with no single authoritative reference covering the preset schema, resolution
order, the `GAME_INFO` convention, or how to author a new preset. The shipped
presets are distribution-oriented (`core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/`deluxe`/`full`);
none selects a *specific named game*, so a developer cannot build or run, for
example, Main Street in isolation from the launcher checkout.

## Users and user stories

- As a **game developer**, I want to build/run one specific game in isolation so
  I can iterate quickly without pulling in the other games, using
  `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id>`.
- As an **engine maintainer**, I want one authoritative document describing how
  build presets are structured, resolved and created, so I can add a preset
  correctly without reverse-engineering the plugin.
- As a **release engineer**, I want the README to keep a concise summary and
  link to the detailed doc, so the high-traffic entry point stays short while
  the full contract is discoverable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. README keeps a concise "Which games does a build include?" section and links
   to a dedicated detailed document (`docs/dev/game-configuration.md`) for full
   details, replacing the current `docs/DEVELOPER.md#config-driven-game-catalogue`
   anchor as the primary reference.
2. The detailed document describes the preset schema in full: the top-level
   `games` array; required `id`, `path`, `scenePath`; optional `adapterPath`,
   `siblingScenePath` and `siblingAdapterPath` (the `src/`-layout sibling
   fields, Option C); the non-schema `$comment` annotation; preset selection
   (`GAMES_CONFIG` preset name or explicit path, default `core-only`); the
   three-step resolution order (`<root>/<scenePath>` →
   `<path>/<siblingScenePath>` → `<path>/<scenePath>`); the always-present
   core-owned Gym; the `GAME_INFO` convention and parsing; and
   validation/failure modes. It explains what each shipped preset (distribution
   and per-game) is and how it is structured — not only one example.
3. A per-game preset exists at `configs/<game-id>.json` for every example game —
   `beleaguered-castle`, `blackjack`, `coloretto`, `feudalism`, `golf`,
   `lost-cities`, `main-street`, `sushi-go` — each containing exactly that one
   game entry (Gym is always added by the plugin).
4. `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id>` selects exactly that game (+ Gym): the generated
   registry for each per-game preset imports the game's scene class and no other
   game, and one representative per-game preset is verified with a real
   `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id> npm run build`.
5. Unit tests guard every per-game preset: each ships exactly one game, uses the
   sibling `../tce-<id>` path form, resolves to a real scene module with the
   expected scene class, and generates a catalogue containing that game + Gym and
   no other game. Existing distribution-preset and discovery-plugin tests still
   pass.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes: the README
   summary section, the `docs/DEVELOPER.md` catalogue section, the new
   `docs/dev/game-configuration.md`, `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`
   where it references `configs/*.json` presets, and the preset/`GAME_INFO`
   doc comment in `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` (which still lists
   the pre-rename preset names `core-only`, `all` and `sample`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not break the existing distribution presets (`core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/
  `deluxe`/`full`) or their tests; per-game presets are additive.
- Presets are data only — no plugin/behaviour change is required (the plugin
  already iterates `games`).
- UK English in all prose.

## Existing state

- Build presets: `configs/{core-only,solo,arcade,deluxe,full}.json`
  (renamed from `core-only/sample/all` in commit `1b6c84b6`).
- Discovery plugin: `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` (`selectConfigPath`,
  `loadGamesConfig`, `discoverGames`, `renderGameRegistryModule`,
  `selectedGameIds`).
- Tests: `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` (a `PRESET_GAMES` map),
  `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts`.
- Docs: `README.md` ("Which games does a build include?"), `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
  ("Config-Driven Game Catalogue"), `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`.
- Known doc drift: the plugin's header doc comment
  (`scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`) still names the pre-rename presets
  `core-only`, `all` and `sample`; correct it to the shipped
  `core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/`deluxe`/`full` set.
- Deployment note: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` currently builds the default
  (`core-only`) preset — covered by the separate work item CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1.

## Desired change

Add eight per-game presets (`configs/<game-id>.json`), add a dedicated
`docs/dev/game-configuration.md` reference, trim/link the README section to it,
and extend the preset tests to cover the per-game set.

## Key Files

- `configs/<game-id>.json` — eight new per-game presets (one game entry each).
- `docs/dev/game-configuration.md` — new authoritative reference for the preset
  schema, resolution, `GAME_INFO` convention and authoring steps.
- `README.md` — concise summary + link to the new doc.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — point the catalogue section at the new doc; keep the
  workflow summary.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — cross-reference the per-game presets
  alongside the existing `configs/*.json` mention.
- `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` — extend `PRESET_GAMES` (or add a
  per-game guard) for the eight per-game presets.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — doc comment cross-reference only
  (no behaviour change expected).

## Related work

- CG-0MTRO6Y2N009B9CF — Config-driven game discovery (Vite plugin + configs/).
- CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC — Launcher distribution with configs/ presets (solo/
  arcade/deluxe/full).
- CG-0MTRO7BFQ003IN2X — Documentation for the multi-repo workflow.
- CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1 — Deploy full engine with all games via `GAMES_CONFIG=all`
  (deployment follow-on).
- CG-0MLVJR7JI0YF87IN — Game Selector: Fix card layout for 4+ games (completed;
  the selector must render the growing per-preset catalogue cleanly).
- CG-0MSKVOSW3004HZVB — Verify full suite green with documented deps (completed;
  establishes the test baseline this change must keep green).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** per-game presets are named `configs/<game-id>.json` (so
  `GAMES_CONFIG=main-street`), matching the `id` used everywhere else.
- **Assumption:** the existing distribution presets are kept as-is; per-game
  presets are additive (`solo.json` remains a golf distribution preset even
  though `configs/golf.json` also selects golf).
- **Risk (low):** preset proliferation / maintenance (13 presets). Mitigated by
  a test that derives the per-game set from the game list rather than hand-listing.
- **Risk (low):** doc drift between README, DEVELOPER.md and the new doc.
  Mitigated by making the new doc the single detailed reference and linking from
  both.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the `deploy.yml` `GAMES_CONFIG` change is out of scope
  here and tracked by CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interview questions were required. Requirements were stated explicitly by
  the operator: (a) keep the README configuration section brief and link to a
  separate document; (b) the separate document must explain how configurations
  are created and structured — not just describe one example preset; (c) create
  one configuration per game so each game can be built in isolation.
- The preset renaming to `solo/arcade/deluxe/full` (commit `1b6c84b6`) landed
  during this session; this brief reflects the post-rename state.

# Task: Create the nine `tce-*` GitHub repositories and push extracted history

## Goal

As a distribution maintainer I can clone each per-game repository
(`tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`,
`tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`) plus
`tableau-card-engine-core` from GitHub with `--recurse-submodules`, then run
`npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit`, and get a runnable
single-game TCE checkout — so the sibling-repo composition that F4/F9 built and
verified **locally** exists on the remote and is cloneable by anyone.

## Users (user stories)

- **Distribution maintainer** — creates the nine remotes **once**, in the final
  F9 Option C `src/` layout, so no history-rewriting re-push is ever needed.
- **Game developer** — `git clone --recurse-submodules
  git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tce-golf.git` and builds/tests the game against
  the engine pulled in as the `core` submodule.
- **Launcher / distribution builder** — composes a subset of the remote game
  repos as siblings (the `solo` and `full` presets) against fresh clones.

## Context

Split out of F4 (CG-0MTRO72W5003ECAK) per operator decision: F4 delivers the
local per-game launcher scaffold (configs, `GAME_INFO`, build/test/package,
history-preserving extraction); creating and pushing the remote repositories is
a separate concern. The F4 producer gate deferred remote creation until the F9
Option C `src/` layout settled, so the nine repos are created **once, in the
final `src/` shape** — no history-rewriting re-push.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The nine repositories exist on GitHub under `TheWizardsCode` at the remotes
   recorded in `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`:
   `tableau-card-engine-core`, `tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`,

   *not* created; `README.md`/`docs/DEVELOPER.md` clone guidance must document

   `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`) pass, and the published remotes

9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No CI pipeline and no npm publication (epic constraint).
- Never rewrite the source monorepo: extraction always operates on a clone
  (`git clone --no-local`); the monorepo `main` is never pushed to directly.
- `git filter-repo` is required and is **not currently installed** on this host

## Plan re-check: closure is incomplete (OPEN QUESTION)

This plan run started while the item was `in_progress` (`stage: intake_complete`). Mid-session the item was closed by another agent (`Map`) at 2026-09-26T16:37:37Z, moving it to `in_progress → completed / in_review` via commit `a341ec3c`.

That closure fixed a **real but latent** defect — the `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` path in `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (it resolved one level above the repo root). It was validated only under `GAMES_CONFIG=full`.

**The failure is not resolved under the default `unit` profile.** Re-verified on `dev` at `a341ec3c`:

```
$ npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts      # GAMES_CONFIG unset
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  4 failed | 12 passed | 5 skipped (21)
 FAIL  Replay CLI -- transcript validation > invalid transcript files > should exit with error for wrong transcript version
        expected 'Error: Could not auto-detect game type from transcript. Available adapters: none. …' to contain 'version'
 FAIL  Replay CLI -- transcript validation > invalid transcript files > should exit with error for missing initialState
        'Error: Unknown game type 'golf'. Available adapters: none'
 FAIL  Replay CLI -- v1 transcript handling > should reject v1 transcript when --stop-at is used
 FAIL  Replay CLI -- v1 transcript handling > should accept v1 transcript for regular replay (no --stop-at)
```

It passes with `GAMES_CONFIG=full` (`npm test`, `npm run test:smoke`, `npm run test:dev`), because those shell runners export `GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"`.

**Root cause:** `scripts/replay.ts` registers adapters from the *active preset* (`registerConfiguredAdapters`). The default preset is `core-only` (`scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts: DEFAULT_PRESET`), which registers **no** adapters, so auto-detection fails. The test spawns the CLI with `env: { ...process.env }` (`tests/golf/replay.test.ts`), so it inherits `core-only` under a bare `npx vitest run --project unit …` and under the project-local `/skill:test --type unit` profile, whose command does **not** export `GAMES_CONFIG`. Only the shell runners (`run-ci-tests.sh`, `run-smoke-tests.sh`, `run-dev-tests.sh`) set it.

**Why it matters:** `/skill:test --type unit` is documented in `AGENTS.md` as the *minimum bar for every change* ("A skill calls for testing → run unit tests"), and `npx vitest run --project unit tests/<game>/` is documented as the targeted per-game command. This is the profile that surfaced the triage item. So the triage is reproducible under the documented developer workflow, even though `npm test` is green.

**OPEN QUESTION (for the producer) — which fix is intended?**

1. **Test-local (recommended, in-repo, surgical):** make `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` hermetic by exporting the preset it needs to the spawned CLI, e.g. `env: { ...process.env, GAMES_CONFIG: process.env.GAMES_CONFIG ?? 'full' }`. Keeps core unit profiles runnable under `core-only` (consistent with `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts` "core test profiles must stay runnable even with a bad `GAMES_CONFIG`").
2. **Profile-level (infrastructure, `.pi/`):** add `GAMES_CONFIG=full` to the `unit` (and `smoke`/`dev`) commands in `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` so they match the shell runners. Per `AGENTS.md`, `.pi/` is out of bounds for agents unless explicitly instructed, so this needs a producer decision.

Because the item is already `completed / in_review` and the two fixes differ materially (one touches only the test, the other changes agent infrastructure), I have **not** reopened it or created a follow-up; that decision is yours.
